players.product: Baidu AI Cloud Infra (GPU cloud and CPU cloud, Qianfan MaaS platform) built on proprietary Kunlunxin AI chips (M100, upcoming M300), plus ERNIE foundation models

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F: Baidu made capital expenditures of RMB12.1 billion (US$1.7 billion) in 2025, 9% of revenue, versus RMB8.1 billion (6%) in 2024 and RMB11.2 billion (8%) in 2023, primarily for the purchase of servers, network equipment and other computer hardware to increase network infrastructure capacity and support Gen-AI research and development inputs. The company says capital expenditures may increase in the future with the expansion and improvement of its network infrastructure and the construction of cloud-computing based data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex RMB12.1 billion (US$1.7 billion), 9% of revenue; 2024 RMB8.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F full-year 2025 results: revenue RMB 129,079 million (RMB 133,125 million in 2024); Baidu General Business revenue RMB 102,485 million (down 2% YoY) and iQIYI RMB 27,290 million (down 7%). Online marketing services revenue fell to RMB 67,837 million from RMB 78,563 million, while 'Others' (mainly cloud services and iQIYI video membership) rose to RMB 61,242 million from RMB 54,562 million. 2025 costs included an impairment loss of RMB16,190 million (US$2,315 million) on a long-lived asset group, booked in Baidu General Business, and the 2025 operating loss was RMB 5,823 million; net income attributable to Baidu was RMB 5,589 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue RMB 129,079 million; Others (incl. cloud) RMB 61,242 million vs RMB 54,562 million; impairment RMB16,190 million

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F supply disclosure: Baidu says it has made significant investments in foundation models and generative AI and made significant prepayments to acquire relevant resources from third-party suppliers (suppliers not named), on whom it relies for consistent and reliable cloud services and other resources necessary for its AI initiatives. On the balance sheet, long-term advances to suppliers rose to RMB 17,997 million at December 31, 2025 from RMB 8,870 million a year earlier, and current advances to suppliers to RMB 5,180 million from RMB 3,048 million (the filing does not break these advances down by supplier or purpose).
quarterly_data.figure: long-term advances to suppliers RMB 17,997 million (RMB 8,870 million a year earlier)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F Apollo Go (robotaxi) international expansion: in July 2025 Apollo Go entered into a multi-year strategic partnership with Uber Technologies, Inc. to deploy thousands of Apollo Go's fully autonomous vehicles on the Uber platform across multiple international markets, with initial deployments planned for Asia and the Middle East; in August 2025 it entered into a strategic partnership with Lyft, Inc. to deploy fully autonomous vehicles across key European markets through the Lyft platform, starting with Germany and the United Kingdom; in October 2025 it partnered with PostBus (Switzerland) on an on-demand autonomous mobility service. In November 2025 Apollo Go received permits for fully driverless commercial operations in Abu Dhabi; in early 2026 it launched fully autonomous ride-hailing services in Abu Dhabi with AutoGo, secured Dubai's first fully driverless testing permit, partnered with Uber to bring Apollo Go to the Uber platform in Dubai, and entered the South Korean market starting with the Seoul metropolitan area.
quarterly_data.figure: thousands of fully autonomous vehicles to be deployed on the Uber platform (multi-year partnership, July 2025)
